Third game developed under the Astro Port banner but only seventh to reach Steam, [b]Meglilo[/b] has the most bizarre premise out of their games: a spin-off of [b]Vulkaiser[/b] where a magical girl, killed while defending the mecha's inventor, is rebuilt by him into a cyborg who fights the Gogoh Army at the same time as Vulkaiser, with a strong dose of dark, cynical humour - see the recurring gag of "Let's wait and see what happens". She even fights a copycat at some point like Vulkaiser did. When a boss fight happens she summons a "Marchen Dimension" that begs many questions about what type of magical kingdom she hails from. The following AP game, ostensibly set in the very same universe thirty or so years later, is [b]Gigantic Army[/b]...

In a gimmick I haven't seen in many shmups to my memory, the heroine has no bombs or other special attacks but rather a warp system that, upon use, stops the action and allows to move instantly where indicated, getting safely out of obstacles and bullet barrages that would otherwise be impossible to avoid. It can't be used indefinitely and recharges faster while not shooting, which can get quite difficult at times as enemies may come even in large swarms; learning to confront as much danger as possible without warping is essential. Due to this gameplay that may force fighting into tight spaces, it's no surprise that collectible weapons are mostly focused on covering the sides.

The graphics are colorful but look even amateurish at times; given that AP had already made [b]Armed Seven[/b] at this point, however, it's clear it's a stylistic choice.

A run of all six levels can be done in 20 minutes but once all lives are lost, there is no continuing; given how combative the final boss can get, it may not be easy to see the end even on Easy. Not one of the developer's best but still a fine little title, with some lack of refinements forgivable given it's one of their earliest.

To my surprise but really not much, I found out that [b]Meglilo[/b] originates from one of the early [b]Dezaemon[/b] productions by the developers. The title tune is similar, the premise of the little witch turned cyborg too, but the enemies... well, look for yourself! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-PuuopE7QpM

WITCH-BOT MEGLILO, developed by ASTRO PORT and published by Henteko Doujin, is a high-energy 2D vertical shoot ’em up that blends classic arcade sensibilities with eccentric sci-fi flair and anime-inspired character design. At first glance, it embraces the familiar structure of traditional bullet hell shooters: waves of enemies flood the screen, projectiles form intricate patterns, and reflexes are tested to their limits. However, beneath that familiar foundation lies a distinctive mobility mechanic and a playful narrative tone that help it stand apart from more conventional entries in the genre.

You take control of Meglilo, a magical-girl-turned-cybernetic-warrior who faces off against the eccentric Gogoh Army and their over-the-top commanders. The story unfolds through short, comedic cutscenes that add personality without interrupting the pace for too long. While the narrative is intentionally absurd and lighthearted, it provides context for the escalating battles and gives the game a unique identity. Rather than presenting a solemn sci-fi epic, WITCH-BOT MEGLILO leans into campy humor and exaggerated character interactions, reinforcing its energetic, arcade-style presentation.

The most defining gameplay feature is Meglilo’s time-stop warp ability. At the press of a button, time briefly freezes and allows her to teleport instantly to another location on the screen. This mechanic transforms the traditional bullet-dodging formula by adding a layer of strategic repositioning. Instead of relying solely on weaving through bullet patterns, players can escape seemingly impossible situations by carefully managing their warp gauge. Because the ability consumes a limited resource that refills gradually, it cannot be used recklessly. Effective play requires balancing conventional movement with tactical teleports, creating a rhythm that feels both reactive and deliberate.

Weapon customization further deepens the experience. Meglilo is accompanied by configurable support satellites mounted on her left and right sides. These satellites can be equipped with different attack types—ranging from focused laser beams to spread shots and close-range drills—allowing players to tailor their offensive strategy. The combination of left and right loadouts significantly influences how you approach each stage. Some setups favor aggressive close-quarters combat, while others emphasize safe, long-range precision. Experimenting with these combinations adds replay value and encourages players to find a playstyle that complements their reflexes and preferences.

Visually, the game embraces colorful pixel art and vibrant bullet patterns that evoke the spirit of classic arcade shooters. Enemy designs are varied and expressive, with bosses occupying large portions of the screen and unleashing dense projectile sequences. Backgrounds shift across stages to reflect changing environments, maintaining visual variety despite the relatively compact campaign length. The soundtrack complements the action with fast-paced, synth-driven tracks that heighten intensity during major encounters. The overall presentation strikes a balance between retro homage and modern indie polish, delivering clarity even during chaotic firefights.

Difficulty scaling is handled through multiple modes, making the game accessible to both newcomers and seasoned shoot ’em up veterans. Lower difficulty levels allow players to enjoy the mechanics and story without overwhelming bullet density, while higher settings significantly increase projectile complexity and enemy aggression. On tougher modes, boss patterns demand memorization, precision timing, and efficient use of the warp mechanic. This scalability ensures that the game can function both as an entry-level bullet hell and as a genuine challenge for experienced players seeking mastery.

Despite its strengths, WITCH-BOT MEGLILO remains a relatively concise experience. The campaign does not span a large number of stages, and players seeking extensive narrative depth may find the story segments brief. However, its arcade-oriented design emphasizes replayability through score chasing, difficulty variation, and loadout experimentation rather than length. The focus is clearly on refining performance and achieving higher scores rather than on prolonged storytelling.

Ultimately, WITCH-BOT MEGLILO stands out as a compact yet inventive shoot ’em up that refreshes traditional bullet hell gameplay with its time-stop teleportation mechanic and customizable weapon system. Its vibrant presentation, energetic pacing, and tongue-in-cheek narrative give it a memorable personality within the genre. For fans of classic arcade shooters who appreciate tight controls and strategic mobility, it offers a focused and replayable experience that rewards both reflexes and tactical thinking.

Rating: 8/10

You know, I'll be happy if all the games I buy for the rest of my life are identical Astro Port games with one unique gameplay mechanic. 

This one is part of their weirdly connected storyline, where all of their games take place, but it's supposed to be a bit more comedic and tongue in cheek than the others. Astro Port is usually inspired by nostalgia, both in terms of subject matter and gameplay; so their library has shmups like Raiden, or shmups inspired by 1970s Super Robots, or side-scrollers inspired by Assault Suits Valken and so on. This is based on... magical girls. Sort of. It's subversive to the trope. Just don't skip the intro sequence the game starts.

Gameplay-wise, it's fine. It's up to Astro Port's usual standard, in terms of both quality and style. If you've played their other shmups, you know what to expect of this one. Its unique gameplay mechanic is the ability to warp to different areas of the screen and reposition yourself. Visuals are fine, colorful, intentionally cartoon-like. Sound's fine too.

The only thing I wish they'd implement already is free play. The training mode doesn't count. Let that 1CC be the goal, not the requirement. Other than that, if you like shmups, pick it up, if only on a sale. Pick up all of their games. Except Saltazius.

Witch-Bot Meglilo has a silly, cutesy but occasionally strangely dark theme, but is a decent vertically scrolling shooter.  It makes use of the same warp mechanics found in one of Astro Port's other titles Zangeki Warp.  Warping being an ability to pause the action and teleport the player character to a different spot controlled by the player to avoid damage and obstacles. But unlike Zangeki Warp, Witch-Bot Meglilo doesn't make the use of warping nearly as much.

The other mechanic at play in Witch-Bot Meglilo is her satellite weapon upgrades.  During the level yellow rockets when destroyed will drop various power ups including additional shields, screen clearing bombs and weapon upgrades.  These weapon upgrades range from changing the direction of her satellite shots to homing missles, area of effect attacks and even a couple of powerful melee weapons.  The real trick being getting the best or favored upgrades for the right or left satellite when it's the most useful.  Melee weapons do a ton of constant damage to bosses, but that damage and short range isn't as effective when swarmed by a horde of enemies.  Likewise, some of the directional shots just aren't shooting at the best angles for some levels.  Fortunately, the chance of changing out upgrades is pretty often.  

The theme of the game of might be a bit of a hang up for some players.  Being a 1970s anime witch girl brought back robocop style by the same scientist that built the giant robot Vulkiaser for another Astro Port title Supercharged Robot Vulkaiser.  Another silly-ish 1970 anime inspired shooter.  However, I would suggest would be players look past the theme to a good, not great shoot em' up.

♪~剧情前述~♪
[i]主角美格莉萝是来自魔法国度的天生魔法少女，某一天为了救下即将被邪恶女干部莉莉大佐轰杀的天护博士而挡刀变成了一团肉泥。热爱超级系萝卜的天护博士为了报答美格莉萝的救命之恩[strike]更可能只是因为眼前有一个趁手的实验样本[/strike]将她改造成了赛博格，从此世间诞生了一个同时有着魔法少女的魔幻系能力和超级系机械人的钢铁之躯的物法双修无敌英雄！但经过一顿忒休斯之船级别的零件替换改造后死而复生的美格莉萝似乎性情大变，几乎丧失了所有人性，这样的她还能继续胜任保护民众，打击邪恶的责任吗...?[/i]

游戏按照传统STG的版面方式划分关卡，在版面开始和结尾加入了儿童剧风格的插图剧情，因为全篇基调就是地狱笑话所以不推荐只是觉得画风可爱就感兴趣的人去游玩[strike]如果还喜欢地狱笑话的话那就更好了！[/strike]

作为STG游戏首先难度亲民，再加上主角还有着魔法少女这个前身带来的，这个游戏种类中颠覆性的特殊机动能力：时间停止+任意传送。而改造为赛博格的她现在还能使用导弹和钻头等升级选项攻击，结合丰富的版面以及美术设计可以说这是一个非常适合新人尝试的STG游戏。而对于高手们游戏也提供了高难模式，此难度下时停瞬移需要合理规划使用。
剧情有，趣味性有，创新有，还很好上手，剩余比较明显的缺点可能是没有continue功能熟练版面通关前可能需要重开几次游戏，就算这样2小时内通关大概还是绰绰有余...?

You should be able to choose which side weapon to change.

Now, you'd think that with its cute art and its focus on the warp mechanic (being invincible to bullets while time stops) the game isn't too hard. Nope, warping consumes your gauge and it recharges slowly over time (faster while you don't shoot). Additionally, mistakes can be very devastating. Also, despite the cute art and silly music, the game's humor is quite morbid. However, it is widely genuinely considered funny, so do take your time to look at the intro and stage cutscenes.

Your only way to gain lives is via score extends and the most efficient way to score is by being in Maximum mode with your shield, which means you collected another shield item while already having 2. Having Maximum shield will provide you with score overtime, unless you fight bosses/mid bosses. If you get hit, you have 1 shield left, which means it will take another 2 shield items without getting hit to get back to Maximum shield.

The weapon system is another very important aspect of the game, especially on higher difficulties. Over the course of the entire game, you can collect weapon items. You can equip a weapon either on your left or your right side, based on how you collect it. If you die both weapons will be replaced by the weapon that was equipped before then on each side. You're also still left with no shields after dying, possibly leaving you in a miserable state to continue your run in. You can not set the weapons you want to start out with when practicing a stage in practice mode, even though it is a totally valid strategy to use some weapons across multiple stages instead of using the weapons the stage gives you at the start.

The two highest difficulties Hard and Insane have multiple patterns not designed to be dodged without the warp mechanic. However, since your usage of it is limited, you're better of destroying many enemies early by having good weapons. Considering all this, it's easy to end up in a nasty downward spiral after dying or even just taking a hit and not having Maximum shields (I have yet to beat Insane).

The two lower difficulties Easy and Normal are vastly easier, however. Patterns are dodgeable and you don't need to be in an ideal state all the time to still stand a chance to clear.

Highly recommended even for non shooter fans.

This is a great intro to bullet hell shooters for newbies or a fun diversion for people who already like them.  Edit: I think anyone will find the 'insane' level has a reasonable quantity of bullets.

#1 tip - DON'T HIT BUTTONS at the '1977' title screen or at the start of new levels, or you'll miss all the 'plot'. Just sit back and laugh your ass off.

Shooting is automatic as long as you hold the shoot key down, enemies are large and colorful, shots stand out well, and there's a time stop and warp mechanism that means that as long as you see the bullet coming you're effectively invincible on easy mode - oh, you'll die a lot to start with if you're new, but once you get the hang of it and of avoiding bullets being the most important thing you'll be okay.  

I've beaten normal mode which is a tad easy for bullet hell (I've beaten Ten and Till in Lowres Kingdom, I know hell), but there are two higher levels I'll be back for when I have more time  And, the huge variation in the optional weapons really changes things up.

Finally, the story is great. Instead of going the mysterious emo route like Touhou or Murasaki (which I love, but the plot is trying way too hard) it just goes for outright absurd and funny.  Character art is done by Shake-O, the guy who draws Doctor Hitomi's Infirmary.  He can draw better than this, but Meglilo is from 1977.

Noob tips:
   * Shooting things is great, but avoiding bullets is your #1 priority.
   * The #2 most important thing is having the right weapon for the area.  If you've got the right weapon things are easy, if you don't it's hell.  When the game gives you powerup drones to shoot, shoot them and take it. It's almost always the right weapon for the next area.
   * Use your warp whenever you need it - it regenerates, and better to use it now and run out later than die now.
   * Pay attention at the start - the game will explicitly introduce you to the concept of the 'hitbox'. Meglilo's head and feet don't count if hit by bullets, only the blinking bit in her back does!
   * Kitchy is mai waifu, get away from her YOU BIT... oh, she's dead. :/
